findings.problem: The same multi-step mathematical argument is written out twice: (i) rewrite the Hilbert inner product `inner ℝ F ψT` via `MeasureTheory.L2.inner_def` into the torus integral of the pointwise pairing (lines 226 and 244–245, both followed by the `simp [mul_comm]` step at 222–225 and 246–249); (ii) rewrite both factor coeFn's using a.e. equalities to `periodicToTorus` of the Euclidean functions and use that `periodicToTorus` is multiplicative (rfl proof at 217–221 and 255–259); (iii) transfer the torus integral to the half-open cell with `integral_periodicToTorus_eq_unitCell` (213 and 260–261) and then to `AVenhance.unitCube` with `integral_unitCell_eq_unitCube` (207–209 and 262–263). In addition, the three-line a.e. identification of the test class, `have htest : (fun x : Torus => ψT x) =ᵐ[volume] AVenhance.Infra.Torus.periodicToTorus ψ := (frozenInitialData_memLp_torus (LimitRepresentation.smoothPeriodicTest_memL2On hψ)).coeFn_toLp`, appears verbatim twice (lines 195–197 as `htest`, lines 239–241 as `hψT`). The two theorems differ only in the torus class `F` (`u t` resp. `P.initialTorusL2`) and the Euclidean representative `g` (`weakPathRepresentative u t` resp. `P.θ₀`), plus the fact that the weak-path statement puts the integral on the left. Roughly twenty lines of real argument (L² inner product ↔ integral, a.e. transport through the periodic transfer, cell/cube transfer) are duplicated, so an API change in the torus integration lemmas or in `smoothPeriodicTestL2` must be fixed in two places, and the two proofs can silently diverge (e.g. one could start from `unitCell` and the other from `unitCube`).
findings.proposed_change:
Extract one lemma carrying the whole calculation, e.g.

```lean
theorem inner_smoothPeriodicTestL2_eq_cell_integral (F : ScalarTorusL2) {g ψ : Vec 2 → ℝ}
    (hg : (fun x : Torus => F x) =ᵐ[volume] AVenhance.Infra.Torus.periodicToTorus g)
    (hψ : ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ψ) (hperiodic : AVenhance.IsZ2Periodic ψ) :
    inner ℝ F (smoothPeriodicTestL2 hψ hperiodic) =
      ∫ x in AVenhance.unitCube, g x * ψ x
```

Proof sketch (one copy of the current reasoning): set `ψT := smoothPeriodicTestL2 hψ hperiodic`, record `hψT : (fun x => ψT x) =ᵐ periodicToTorus ψ` from `MemLp.coeFn_toLp`; expand `L2.inner_def`, rewrite `inner ℝ (F x) (ψT x)` to `F x * ψT x`, fold the product using the definitional multiplicativity of `periodicToTorus` together with `hg` and `hψT` (after `.symm`), then apply `AVenhance.Infra.Torus.integral_periodicToTorus_eq_unitCell` and `AVenhance.Infra.Torus.integral_unitCell_eq_unitCube`. Rewritten uses under the actual hypotheses of this file:
* `weakPathRepresentative_pairing_eq_inner u t hψ hperiodic` (lines 188–226) becomes `(inner_smoothPeriodicTestL2_eq_cell_integral (u t) ?hg hψ hperiodic).symm`, where `?hg : (fun x : Torus => u t x) =ᵐ periodicToTorus (weakPathRepresentative u t)` is obtained pointwise from `periodicToTorus_fromUnitTorus (fun y : Torus => u t y)` applied to the current `hrep` (lines 200–205); the goal is stated with the integral on the left, hence `.symm`.
* `FrozenDriftProblem.initial_pairing_eq_cell_integral P hψ hperiodic` (lines 230–263) becomes exactly `inner_smoothPeriodicTestL2_eq_cell_integral P.initialTorusL2 hθ hψ hperiodic`, reusing the existing `hθ` of lines 236–238; the duplicated `hψT` at 239–241 disappears.
(I could not compile this proposal.)
findings.benefit: The L²-pairing/periodic-transfer calculation is stated and proved once, so both theorems reduce to instantiating a single lemma with the torus class and representative as parameters; the a.e. identification of `smoothPeriodicTestL2` with `periodicToTorus ψ` is computed once instead of twice. A reader sees immediately that both statements share the same mathematical content (and that the weak-path version is only the symmetric form of the initial-data version), and future changes to the torus integration API (`integral_periodicToTorus_eq_unitCell`, `integral_unitCell_eq_unitCube`, `smoothPeriodicTestL2`) require one proof update. It also gives later files that need the same identification (cf. the re-derived a.e. lemmas `ProductWeakGradient.smoothPeriodicTestL2_coeFn` and `ScalarFourierDerivative.smoothPeriodicTestL2_ae_periodicToTorus`) a canonical, reusable statement.
